analysis.title: Piper Sandler Cos. (PIPR): Modestly weaker near-term revenue trajectory, but long-term story remains intact
key_insights: GS rates PIPR Buy with a 12m price target of $78 (was $80), a 3% cut, against a $68.72 price (13.5% upside). The target uses a 13.5x P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS (4Q27E-3Q28E), rolled forward one quarter.
PIPR reported adjusted 3Q26 EPS of $0.87, below GSe of $0.91 and Visible Alpha consensus of $0.93. Revenue was 2% lower than expected and operating margin was about 20bps weaker.
The stock fell 9% on the day of earnings as of publication. GS attributes this to a weak backdrop for investment banking stocks that day plus muted 4Q26 guidance.

4Q26 guidance: Advisory down YoY (Street +4% YoY), Corporate financing down QoQ (Street +7% QoQ), Fixed income flat QoQ (Street -14% QoQ), Equities and Muni financing up QoQ. Muni financing is guided to improve modestly QoQ vs Street +83% QoQ.
Management implied a substantial QoQ step down in non-comp expense in 4Q26.
GS cuts 2026E/27E/28E total revenue by 4%/2%/1% and EPS by 9%/8%/6%. Operating margins fall by 70bps/50bps/30bps.

Investment banking revenue was $332mn in 3Q26, 4% below consensus and +1% YoY. Management expects 4Q26 to be the strongest quarter of the year on a healthy pipeline and private capital momentum. GS cuts 2026E/27E/28E investment banking by 5%/3%/2%.

Equities revenue was $54mn, down 13% QoQ and 4% below the Street, as volumes fell with lower volatility after a strong 2Q26. Program trading rose and the company is expanding into electronic trading. It guided to 4Q26 equities improving QoQ on a European trading launch (Street +15% QoQ).

Fixed income came in 20% above the Street and up 23% QoQ on higher yields and rate volatility, driven by municipal tax-loss swaps, balance sheet optimization and depository hedging. GS raises 2026E/27E/28E fixed income revenue by 8%/3%/2%.
The adjusted comp ratio was 61.5%, flat QoQ and at the low end of the 61.5-62.5% guidance range. GS raises its 2026E comp ratio by 20bps to 61.5%.
Adjusted operating margin was 19.8%, about 20bps below the Street, on a non-comp ratio about 30bps higher. Non-comp expense was $85mn (+9% YoY) on occupancy, litigation and tech consulting fees.

Management expects the 2026 non-comp ratio to be higher YoY on the NYC headquarters build, litigation and tech costs. GS puts the 2026E non-comp ratio at 17.1%, up about 35bps YoY. GS expects non-comp headwinds to fade by mid-2027.

Business mix: sustained depository M&A with an active 1H27 closing backlog but no significant pickup yet. Sponsor M&A is recovering slowly, with higher rates a headwind. Energy M&A is at record momentum (+100% YoY deal completions) on AI data center power demand. Healthcare is broad-based and expected to become the largest business this year. Private capital advisory continues to build.
Municipal financing was 42% below the Street as elevated yields stalled refundings and delayed projects. GS expects a measured recovery as issuers adjust to multi-decade-high yields.
Valuation: the stock trades at 12.0x 2027 GSe adjusted earnings, around the 35th percentile of the past 5 years. GS also says the variable comp model limits downside comp ratio risk.
Price performance: PIPR is down 6.9% over 3m, 20.4% over 6m and 15.8% over 12m, trailing the S&P 500 by 11.8, 26.5 and 24.8 points.

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut 3% to $78 from $80 after a 3Q26 EPS miss, weaker 4Q26 guidance and estimate cuts. GS stays Buy on pipelines, a variable comp model and valuation.

sector_views.rationale: Mixed near-term picture. Energy, healthcare and private capital advisory are strong, depository M&A backlog is active, and sponsor M&A and muni financing are slow because of high rates.

earnings_insights: PIPR 3Q26 adjusted EPS $0.87 reported vs GSe $0.91 and Visible Alpha consensus $0.93, on revenue 2% below expectations.

3Q26 investment banking revenue $332mn reported, 4% below consensus and +1% YoY. Equities revenue $54mn reported, -13% QoQ and 4% below the Street. Fixed income was 20% above the Street and +23% QoQ. Muni financing was 42% below the Street.
3Q26 adjusted comp ratio 61.5% reported (guidance range 61.5-62.5%). Adjusted operating margin 19.8% reported. Non-comp expense $85mn reported, +9% YoY.

4Q26 company guidance versus Street estimates: Advisory down YoY (Street +4% YoY), Corporate financing down QoQ (Street +7% QoQ), Fixed income flat QoQ (Street -14% QoQ), Muni financing modestly up QoQ (Street +83% QoQ), Equities brokerage up QoQ (Street +15% QoQ).

GS estimates, not reported: 2026E/27E/28E diluted EPS (pre-exceptionals) $4.24/$5.17/$5.99, down from $4.65/$5.62/$6.38. 2026E/27E/28E revenue $2,003.8mn/$2,264.5mn/$2,456.3mn. 2025 diluted EPS was $4.44 reported (the old-estimate table shows $4.43).
risk_factors: Slower than expected growth in investment banking and trading.
Longer time to completion pushing out M&A and restructuring revenue.
Giving up prior market share gains.
A large cash build-up dragging on returns.
Higher interest rates weighing on sponsor M&A and municipal financing.
Non-comp expense pressure from the NYC headquarters build, litigation and tech costs.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong deal pipelines, growth in private capital advisory and DCM, energy and healthcare strength, a variable comp model that limits comp ratio downside, non-comp headwinds fading by mid-2027, and a 12.0x 2027E P/E around the 35th percentile of the past 5 years.
tension_points.bear_case: 3Q26 EPS missed, 4Q26 guidance was below the Street for Advisory, Corporate financing and Muni financing, sponsor M&A is held back by rates, and non-comp costs are rising on the NYC headquarters, litigation and tech.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slower than expected growth in IBanking and trading, weaker M&A backlogs, or longer completion times pushing out M&A and restructuring revenue.

theme_stances.key_argument: Near-term revenue is weaker, but the long-term story is intact on pipelines, a variable comp model and valuation.
theme_stances.evidence: we remain constructive on the longer term PIPR story
